subject.title: `doctor --fix` silently drops the `plugins.allow` entry for a bundled→externalized plugin (codex), unregistering the agent harness — and the gateway still reports healthy

question: Should a missing harness required by one or more configured agents degrade global gateway readiness, or be reported as an agent-scoped capability failure while gateway liveness stays healthy?
rationale: The allowlist deletion is a mechanical regression, but global readiness semantics affect unrelated agents, channels, service supervisors, and operator automation and cannot be chosen safely from the issue alone.

options.title: Agent-scoped degraded readiness
options.body: Keep liveness healthy but make detailed readiness, status, and doctor fail visibly with affected agent ids and an in-product install/fix path.

options.title: Fail global readiness
options.body: Mark the whole gateway unready whenever any configured agent references an unavailable harness, prioritizing strict deployment detection over partial availability.

options.title: Doctor-only enforcement
options.body: Repair or block the configuration in doctor and startup while leaving gateway readiness semantics unchanged.

recommendation.title: Agent-scoped degraded readiness
recommendation.body: Keep liveness healthy but make detailed readiness, status, and doctor fail visibly with affected agent ids and an in-product install/fix path.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior merged doctor work defines the closest existing policy for configured runtime plugins that are unavailable.
